title: Injective abelian sheaves on a site have trivial higher Cech cohomology
statement: Let C : Type u be a category with hom universe v, and let the site precoverage J have isomorphisms, composition stability, base-change stability and covering pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every covering family indexed by T : Type (max u v), with chosen fibre products [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], and every injective abelian sheaf I valued in AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}, positive Cech cohomology is zero and degree-zero Cech cohomology is isomorphic to I(U). The coefficient universe contains the objects and homs of C, as required for exact sheafification and cofree presheaves.

proof.text: Exact sheafification and its adjunction transfer injectivity to the underlying presheaf. Use the natural monomorphism into Presheaf.cofree and factor the identity through it by injectivity; functoriality of the chosen Cech complex gives a retraction of complexes.

The cofree complex is exact at each positive degree by the insertion contraction. Map a cocycle into it, obtain a primitive, and map that primitive back through the retraction. The chain-map equations and retraction equation identify its differential with the original cocycle. ExactAt gives IsZero homology.
Apply the degree-zero sheaf gluing identification.

split_report.summary: Split the general-site statement along Stacks 03AW. The proof first transfers injectivity from sheaves to presheaves through the exact sheafification adjunction, then constructs the free Cech presheaf complex and proves its positive-degree exactness by decomposing each value into contractible complexes on the sets of lifts over a fixed map to U. Yoneda identifies Hom from this complex with the Cech complex, and injectivity makes every positive cocycle a coboundary. The sheaf equalizer condition gives the degree-zero identification. The proof uses only the general site and Cech definitions; no small-etale specialization or new node was introduced. Mathlib searches found no Cech-acyclicity theorem for injective sheaves.

old_proof.text: Write PAb(C) for presheaves of abelian groups and let I be the given injective sheaf. The inclusion Ab(C) into PAb(C) has sheafification as an exact left adjoint: finite limits are sectionwise and sheafification preserves finite limits and colimits. Therefore an extension problem from a monomorphism of presheaves into I sheafifies to an extension problem between sheaves, which is solved by injectivity of I; composing the extension with the unit of sheafification gives an extension in presheaves. Thus I is injective in PAb(C).

old_proof.text: Let K_p be the direct sum of the free presheaves Z_{U_t0 x_U ... x_U U_tp} over tuples of covering indices, with alternating face differential. At an object W, decompose K_p(W) by the composite phi: W -> U. The summand for phi is the free abelian group on S_phi^(p+1), where S_phi is the disjoint union of lifts W -> U_t over phi. Face maps delete one entry. If S_phi is empty the summand is zero; otherwise choosing s in S_phi gives the contracting homotopy (s0,...,sp) -> (s,s0,...,sp) in positive degrees. Hence K is exact in every positive degree as a presheaf.

old_proof.text: For every presheaf G, Yoneda identifies Hom(Z_V,G) with G(V), naturally in V and G. Hom out of a direct sum is a product, so Hom(K_p,G) is the product of G on the iterated fibre products; precomposition with a face is restriction along the corresponding projection. The resulting cochain differential is exactly the Cech differential, so Hom(K,I) is the Cech complex of I.

old_proof.text: For p>0, a cocycle s: K_p -> I vanishes on im(d_{p+1}) = ker(d_p), hence factors through B = im(d_p) included in K_{p-1}. Injectivity of I in presheaves extends B -> I to K_{p-1} -> I, whose composite with d_p is s. Every positive-degree cocycle is therefore a coboundary, and Cech H^p(U,I)=0.

old_proof.text: In degree zero, a Cech cocycle is a section of I(U) whose restrictions to every pairwise fibre product agree. The sheaf condition identifies these compatible families with the unique section on U, giving Cech H^0(U,I)=I(U).
